subject: Egress & tenant segmentation — private deployment handoff

Subject: Private deploy: egress+tenant segmentation details for handoff

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we prep for the private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge) we need a concise checklist of the network and security artifacts your team requires from us to complete the operational handoff. Two specific asks from our side:

- Clear egress policy requirements (IP ranges, DNS allowlist vs proxy, TLS inspection guidance).
- Suggested tenant segmentation mapping for our infra team — we have 6 service clusters and two customer production tenants.

Can you confirm the minimum artifacts you need, any templates, and whether Redwood needs VPN or direct interconnect for the first-week cutover? Our IT lead Nitin Gupta (cc'd) will own the network delivery.

Also please include any preferred filenames/formats for import (CSV, Terraform snippets, etc.).

Appreciate a short checklist we can act on — procurement timelines are on a tight cadence so if we can close this by next Wednesday that helps.

Best,
Alex
Head of Cloud Integrations
Nimbus Systems

Subject: Re: Private deploy: egress+tenant segmentation details for handoff

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a pragmatic handoff checklist and the formats we prefer. I kept it intentionally concise for your ops team to act on immediately.

Redwood minimum network & onboarding artifacts (priority order):

1) Egress policy spec (required)
   - Preferred format: PDF or YAML + optional CSV for IP ranges.
   - Fields we need: egress CIDR list, FQDN allowlist, proxy IP (if present), TLS inspection? (yes/no), expected outbound ports (TCP/UDP), peak concurrent connections estimate.
   - If you use an outbound proxy, include a test URL we can curl from the appliance.

2) Tenant segmentation mapping (required)
   - Preferred format: CSV or Excel. Columns: service_cluster_id, cluster_role (api/worker/cache), tenant_assigned (prod/staging), network_zone, minimum_bandwidth_mbps, notes.

3) DNS & routing details (required)
   - Split-horizon DNS entries, internal FQDNs used by your infra, and whether internal clients resolve Redwood endpoints directly.

4) Service account & IAM mapping (required)
   - List of service principals, cert rotation windows, short-lived token TTL preferences.

5) VPN/interconnect decision (nice-to-have upfront)
   - We support both. For initial cutover we recommend direct interconnect (lower latency, predictable throughput). VPN is acceptable if interconnect lead time is an issue — we will need MTU and keepalive settings.

6) Firewall & IDS expectations (nice-to-have)
   - Any inline IDS/IPS that could block gRPC/HTTP2 traffic. If present, provide test windows to validate post-deploy.

7) Contact & escalation matrix (required)
   - Primary/secondary contacts for networking, security, and SRE for the 72-hour cutover window.

Deliverables we will provide back before go-live:
- Redwood egress-policy-draft.pdf (editable) — will include recommended ranges and sample iptables/ACLs.
- Tenant segmentation template (CSV) for you to populate.
- Preflight checklist we run from our side and ask you to confirm.

I attached the initial draft egress policy and a tenant mapping template for your team to populate. If you can fill the tenant CSV and confirm whether you prefer interconnect vs VPN by EOD Friday (20 Nov), we can lock the cutover plan.

Thanks — cc'ing Laura for compliance/controls signoff on the egress guidance.

— Vivek
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Alex / team — quick compliance notes to complement Vivek's checklist: 

- Please ensure the tenant mapping explicitly marks any PII-bearing services. Those clusters will require encrypted-at-rest verification and an HSM/KMS integration window.
- For egress allowlists, include CIDR and (if applicable) ASN notation for your BGP peers. We validate against our SOC 2 approved list.
- If you expect any cross-tenant peering, document the intent and the business justification for audit purposes.

I've attached a short checklist we use during compliance review — it lists the minimal evidence items (KMS ARNs, audit log retention policy, sample logs demonstrating denied egress) we will request during the final review.

Monica — can you add a one-paragraph on certificate rotation windows we recommend?

Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

2) Procurement to confirm interconnect lead time — tentative preference is direct interconnect, will update by EOD Monday.

Appreciate the clear artifacts and quick turnaround.
